subject: Re: Competitive packaging & value-bridge proposal for LatticeWorks
messages:
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@latticeworks.com>
To: mina_haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@latticeworks.com>
Date: 2025-06-11T15:02:00Z
Subject: Competitive pricing request: replacing CloudRunr

Hi Mina,

Thanks for taking this. We are evaluating a vendor replacement for our inference stack currently on CloudRunr and need a concrete value bridge to present to our procurement committee next week. High level ask: can Redwood match the blended economics we have today and outline packaging alternatives if you can not match line for line?

What would be most useful to us: a) a line-item comparison for compute and storage, b) an option with a dedicated capacity bucket for weekday peak hours, and c) a short pilot credit we can use to validate latency at our TPS.

I attached our current contract summary and last month bill. If you can get back with a provisional offer by Thursday 6/12 that would keep us on track.

Thanks,
Ethan
Ethan Cole
Head of Platform Engineering
LatticeWorks

Attachment: lattice-current-contract-summary.pdf (pdf, 210KB)

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@latticeworks.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, connor_obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-12T09:32:00Z
Subject: Re: Competitive pricing request: replacing CloudRunr

Ethan,

Appreciate the packet, and great context. Quick notes up front: we can put together a value bridge that compares your current spend to a few Redwood packaging options. To scope the comparisons properly we need two quick things from you: 1) 7 day p95 latency and p50 token distribution for your peak API; and 2) expected commit horizon (monthly vs 12 month).

Provisional thinking (high level):
- Dedicated capacity during 9am-6pm PST is feasible as a tiered bucket rather than per-hour billing; that helps keep unit cost lower during off-peak.
- We can offer pilot credits for a 4-6 week sandbox that includes dedicated capacity for the pilot window.
- If you need strict parity on KV cache semantics for stateful chat workloads we have a migration checklist; that increases initial onboarding effort but preserves inference quality.

I attached a provisional match worksheet with two packaging scenarios: seat-based bundle and commit-discount. This is not final pricing, but it should be a useful starting point for procurement. Connor, can you review the KV cache note below and flag any migration caveats?

Next steps: Ethan, send the 7-day telemetry and confirm the commit horizon and SLA must-haves. I will follow up with numeric scenarios by end of day Thursday.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachment: redwood-provisional-match.pdf (xls/pdf stub)

From: Connor OBrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@latticeworks.com>
Date: 2025-06-13T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Competitive pricing request: replacing CloudRunr

Mina, Ethan,

Quick technical read on the KV cache and weekday-dedicated bucket ask. Short summary:
- KV semantics: Redwood preserves key-value cache behavior but the TTLing and eviction policy between backends can cause small delta in cold-start token counts. If you have long-running chat sessions with large context windows we recommend an initial mapping step to identify hot prefixes.
- Dedicated capacity for 9-6 PST is straightforward; we recommend a small amount of burst capacity for the first 2 weeks of live to absorb warm-up spikes.
- Migration effort estimate: 2 engineers full time for 3 weeks for data mapping, model pinning, and canary testing. We can provide a migration-checklist and runbook.

I attached the migration checklist and added a column for risk and estimated owner (Dev vs Infra).

Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com

Attachment: migration-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@latticeworks.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@latticeworks.com>
Date: 2025-06-15T14:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Competitive pricing request: replacing CloudRunr

Mina,

Thanks for the quick replies and Connor's notes. A few clarifications from procurement and platform:
- Packaging preference: if you have a seat-based bundle we will evaluate it, but procurement favors a committed usage model with a monthly billing cadence.
- Dedication requirement: we need the dedicated bucket to guarantee 99th p99 latency under a 250 TPS sustained peak window between 9am-5pm ET.
- Pilot credit: procurement is asking for a 3-week pilot with dedicated capacity and access to your Console tracing and token-level cost breakdown.

If you can map those asks into a single comparative table that shows our current line items vs Redwood's commit and seat options, plus the expected migration runway (timeline and engineer days), that will help. Also share any legal/contractual differences we should highlight in the procurement memo.

Attached our last month bill for reference.

Best,
Ethan

Attachment: lattice-current-bill.pdf (pdf, 120KB)

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@latticeworks.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, connor_obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, legal <legal@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-18T10:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Competitive packaging & value-bridge proposal for LatticeWorks

Ethan,

Thanks again for the detail and patience while we pulled internal approvals. Summary of what Redwood can offer to match the ask and minimize uplift risk:

1) Commercial bridge (12 month commit)
- 10% off list on the compute and inference unit price with a 12 month minimum commitment.
- Dedicated weekday bucket sized to meet 250 TPS p99 target during 9am-5pm ET. We will reserve burst capacity for the first 4 weeks.

2) Packaging alternatives
- Seat-based bundle: includes 5 admin seats, console access, and 4 weeks of dedicated pilot credits. This is priced slightly higher but shortens the procurement review.
- Commit-based bundle: lower unit price, requires a PO and a 30 day payment term.

3) Pilot and migration
- We can provide a 6 week pilot with dedicated capacity, Console tracing, and token-level cost reports. Pilot instrumentation and two runbook sessions included.
- Migration runbook estimate matches Connor's note: 2 engineers for approximately 3 weeks. We will supply a detailed cutover plan.

4) Legal and procurement notes
- Standard SOW + Master Subscription Agreement. We can accept a redline to our MSA; typical negotiation points we see are data retention and breach notification timelines. If you prefer we can provide a redline window and a short summary of change impacts for procurement.

Next steps:
- If this aligns, please confirm commit term preference (12 month commit vs seat bundle) and we will issue a consolidated comparison table and a draft PO-ready quote by EOD Monday 6/23.
- For procurement, contact: legal@redwood.com and billing@redwood.com.

I pulled priyom in to own the commercial paperwork and Connor for migration scoping.

Best regards,
Mina Haddad
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142
